items.title: FLOWPROMOTE: rosuvastatin 40 mg plus ezetimibe regresses more coronary plaque than atorvastatin 40 mg in statin-naive stable CAD (JAMA Cardiology)
items.summary: In a prespecified secondary analysis of the FLOWPROMOTE randomised trial (104 statin-naive patients with stable CAD on CT angiography), rosuvastatin 40 mg plus ezetimibe 10 mg lowered LDL-C by 65% vs 38% with atorvastatin 40 mg and produced greater 18-month regression of total plaque volume (-21.1% vs -13.6% with atorvastatin; P=.02) and noncalcified plaque volume across the whole coronary tree.
items.area: Preventive cardiology · Lipid lowering & plaque regression
bullets: **FLOWPROMOTE**: multicentre RCT, prespecified secondary imaging analysis, **JAMA Cardiology, 30 Oct 2026**. Statin-naive, newly diagnosed stable CAD (CT stenosis >50% and **FFR-CT ≤0.80**); coronary CTA at baseline, 9 and 18 months.
**N = 104** (52 per arm; mean age 64, 79% male). Randomised to **atorvastatin 40 mg** ('intensive') or **rosuvastatin 40 mg + ezetimibe 10 mg** ('more intensive') for 18 months.
LDL-C fell from 119.7 to **69.5 mg/dL (-38%)** with atorvastatin vs 127.4 to **42.5 mg/dL (-65%)** with rosuvastatin + ezetimibe (P<.001).
Total plaque volume at 18 months: **-13.6% with atorvastatin vs -21.1% with rosuvastatin + ezetimibe** (difference **-30.9 mm³**, 95% CI -57.2 to -4.5; **P=.02**).
Noncalcified plaque: **-20.0% vs -28.2%** (difference -28.9 mm³, 95% CI -53.2 to -4.6; P=.02); NCPV regressed in **77% vs 98%** of patients (P=.001). Calcified plaque rose similarly in both arms.

Lower achieved LDL-C was **linearly associated** with greater plaque regression; the authors say this supports the potential for **partial reversal** of coronary atherosclerosis with intensive lipid lowering.

Limitations: **small, secondary imaging endpoints**; CT-measured plaque is a **surrogate**, with no clinical outcomes. For context (not from this paper), ESC/EAS goals for very-high-risk patients are **LDL-C <55 mg/dL (<1.4 mmol/L)** and ≥50% reduction.
